v1.feedback: The hiraeth concept lands well — oldest cells detaching and drifting upward as ghost motes is a legible metaphor, and the warm-core-to-cold-periphery gradient sells the longing/distance axis. The parent Lomas cellular morphogenesis is clearly still the structural backbone, not a fresh start. Two things to tighten: the ghost motes use additive blending that reads a bit sparkly/particle-effect rather than melancholic — try a softer normal-blend with lower opacity and a slight blur (larger point size, steeper gaussian falloff) so they feel like fading memories, not fireflies. Also the camera is fixed at z=8 while the form keeps growing; after ~30s the organism risks filling the frame unevenly — a slow dolly-out or adaptive FOV tied to the bounding radius would keep the composition balanced as the body matures.

v2.feedback: The hiraeth concept lands well — cells aging out and drifting upward as cooling ghosts is a legit morphological expression of longing/loss, not just a palette swap. The warm-to-cold color transition on detached motes is restrained and reads clearly. Two issues: the organism's core form is still fundamentally the parent's icosahedral growth without enough visible structural change — hiraeth should warp the growth pattern itself (e.g., asymmetric nutrient bias, elongated reaching tendrils), not just add a particle effect on top. Also the ghost motes at 0.45 max alpha are almost too subtle on the dark background; bump to ~0.55 and consider a faint vertical streak or trail behind each rising ghost to strengthen the 'letting go' read at a glance.
